extracted.intended_audience: public relations practitioners, students, organizational communicators, and stakeholders seeking guidance on the role and functions of PR
extracted.subtask_description: A high-level professional overview of what public relations is and the core functions, responsibilities, and disciplines that constitute PR practice for organizations and practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of public relations (PRSA 1982 and modern)
rubrics_metrics.description: 1982 PRSA definition: “Public relations helps an organization and its publics adapt mutually to each other.” Modern definition: “Public relations is a strategic communication process that builds mutually beneficial relationships between organizations and their publics.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions frame PR as a strategic, two-way, relationship-focused communication activity rather than merely press agentry or publicity; use these definitions as touchstones when assessing whether work emphasizes mutual adaptation, strategic planning, and relationship-building.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core purpose: influence, engagement, and relationship-building
rubrics_metrics.description: At its core, public relations is about influencing, engaging and building a relationship with key stakeholders across numerous platforms in order to shape and frame the public perception of an organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate PR efforts by whether they actively influence stakeholder perceptions, foster engagement, and cultivate ongoing relationships across appropriate platforms rather than solely broadcasting messages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipating, analyzing and interpreting public opinion, attitudes and issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipating, analyzing and interpreting public opinion, attitudes and issues that might have an impact, for good or ill, on the operations and plans of the organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality PR work demonstrates continuous environmental scanning and insight generation—identifying trends, risks, and opportunities in public sentiment and translating them into actionable advice or program adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counseling management on policy, actions and communications (including crisis communications)
rubrics_metrics.description: Counseling management at all levels in the organization with regard to policy decisions, courses of action and communications — including crisis communications — taking into account their public ramifications and the organization’s social or citizenship responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess PR by its advisory role: does it provide management with timely, ethically informed counsel that considers public impact, legal/policy consequences, and corporate responsibility, especially during crises?

rubrics_metrics.name: Protecting the organization’s reputation
rubrics_metrics.description: Protecting the reputation of an organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reputation stewardship is a central metric: effective PR anticipates reputational threats, mitigates damage, and proactively builds goodwill through consistent, authentic communication and stakeholder engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Researching, conducting and evaluating programs of action and communications on a continuing basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Researching, conducting and evaluating, on a continuing basis, programs of action and communications to achieve the informed public understanding necessary to the success of an organization’s aims. These may include marketing; financial; fundraising; employee, community or government relations; and other programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate campaigns and programs on whether they are research-based, implemented systematically, and assessed continuously—across functional areas such as marketing, investor relations, fundraising, and internal communications—for measurable understanding and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planning and implementing efforts to influence or change public policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Planning and implementing the organization’s efforts to influence or change public policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When PR involves public policy, assess the clarity of objectives, alignment with organizational strategy, ethical/legal compliance, stakeholder mapping, and the effectiveness of tactics in shaping policy outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managing resources: objectives, planning, budgeting, staffing, training, and facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Setting objectives, planning, budgeting, recruiting and training staff, developing facilities — in short, managing the resources needed to perform all of the above.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-quality PR functions demonstrate sound management practices: clear objectives, realistic budgets, appropriate staffing and training, and infrastructure that enable sustained communication programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overseeing content creation to drive engagement and leads
rubrics_metrics.description: Overseeing the creation of content to drive customer engagement and generate leads.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess content efforts by strategic alignment (audience, message, channel), quality and relevance of creative, and whether content is optimized to produce measurable engagement and lead generation outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core disciplines and functions within PR
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplines/functions within PR include: Corporate Communications; Crisis Communications; Executive Communications; Internal Communications; Investor Relations Communications; Marketing Communications; Integrated Marketing/Integrated Marketing Communications; Media Relations; Content Creation; Events; Social Media; Multimedia; Reputation Management; Speechwriting; Brand Journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these functional categories to classify work, assign responsibility, and set specific success metrics—recognizing that each discipline has its own methods and KPIs but should align with overarching PR strategy.
